 De’Aaron Fox (hip) is questionable to play against the Warriors on Friday. 
 Fox could end up missing a game for the first time this season. If that happens, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle would likely see a bump in usage. Devin Vassell has been sidelined but is questionable as well. If he returns and Fox is out, Julian Champagnie will continue to start. If both are out, Keldon Johnson or Carter Bryant could enter the starting lineup. 
 De'Aaron Fox 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #4 
 De’Aaron Fox recorded 17 points (7-of-17 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, nine assists, three steals and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Bulls. 
 Matching his season high in assists, Fox finished Wednesday’s victory one helper shy of a double-double. Add in the steals, and this was a decent night for those rostering the Spurs guard. Fox entered the season with a seventh-round ADP in nine-cat formats, and his production has aligned with that expectation. 
 De'Aaron Fox 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #4 
 De’Aaron Fox recorded 15 points (5-of-8 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), nine rebounds, six assists and two three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Suns. 
 Like backcourt partner Dylan Harper, Fox’s production has aligned with his ADP thus far. He didn’t record any defensive stats against the Suns, but the Spurs’ guard shot the ball well and finished one rebound shy of a double-double. This could be a good week for Fox, as three of the Spurs’ four games (Phoenix, Chicago and Utah) are against teams with losing records. 
 De'Aaron Fox 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #4 
 De’Aaron Fox finished Saturday’s win over the Timberwolves with 22 points (8-of-10 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), eight rebounds, seven assists and one block. 
 Fox had his best game of the season thus far, recording his first 20-point game while shooting 80 percent from the field. For the season, Fox is shooting 57.6 percent from the field and 80 percent from the foul line, and that efficiency has boosted his fantasy value. 
 De'Aaron Fox 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #4 
 De’Aaron Fox finished Saturday’s win over the Mavericks with 19 points (6-of-11 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), three rebounds, nine assists, three steals, one block and two three-pointers. 
 One night after scoring 19 points in a loss to the Rockets, Fox matched that mark against the Mavericks on Saturday. The veteran point guard also recorded nine assists in a second straight game, bringing his total to 25 over three games. After committing five turnovers against the Rockets, Fox committed two against the Mavericks. The Spurs play three games in Week 2, starting with the Kings on Tuesday. 
 De'Aaron Fox 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #4 
 De’Aaron Fox (wrist) is available for Friday’s game against the Rockets. 
 Fox’s sprained right wrist will not keep him out of Friday’s game. He’ll take on his usual starting point guard duties as the Spurs look to rebound from Tuesday’s loss to the Thunder. 
 De'Aaron Fox 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #4 
 De’Aaron Fox (wrist) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Rockets. 
 Fox, who played 32 minutes in Tuesday’s season-opening loss to the Thunder, is dealing with a sprained right wrist. If there’s a silver lining to the injury, it’s that he shoots left-handed. If Fox can’t play on Friday, Julian Champagnie could move into the starting lineup after playing 30 minutes off the bench on Tuesday. 
 De'Aaron Fox 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #4 
 De’Aaron Fox posted a strong line on Tuesday with 14 points (6-of-9 FGs), seven rebounds, seven assists and one steal against the Thunder. 
 Despite being written off after a rough Finals series, Fox is still a productive player, which he showcased in this game. He’ll continue to be an important piece for the Spurs this season, even if they continue to start all three of their guards. Fox led the Spurs in assists in this game after Stephon Castle led the team in dimes last season. If Fox is the primary playmaker this year for San Antonio, he may see a nice boost in production. 
 Victor Wembanyama 
 SAS 
 Forward-Center 
 #1 
 The San Antonio Spurs will start DeAaron Fox, Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper, Devin Vassell, and Victor Wembanyama on Friday against the Kings. 
 Jeff McDonald also reported that coach Mitch Johnson intends to use this starting lineup on Tuesday against the Thunder. The Spurs will use their three guard lineup with Champagnie and Harris coming off the bench. We’ll see if the starting lineup sticks that way beyond this upcoming Tuesday, but you can feel good to draft Vassell to stream him in on opening night. 
 De'Aaron Fox 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #4 
 De’Aaron Fox recorded nine points (3-of-5 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), three rebounds, four assists and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Suns. 
 Wednesday’s exhibition was the first of the preseason for Fox, who logged 19 minutes against the Suns. While he struggled during the NBA Finals, the Spurs’ point guard is locked into that role going into the 2026-27 season. Fox may not be a top-50 fantasy player, but he remains valuable to managers willing to punt free-throw percentage.

 Keyonte George had himself a night with 27 points (8-of-17 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, a steal, and four 3-pointers in loss on Friday. 
 It was trending towards being a bad Keyonte George game after the first half. He really got going with 23 points in the second half which helped the Jazz stay in the game once the Rockets started to make shots. He’s been awesome this season his ability to take a leadership role on this team is much needed.

 Darryn Peterson put up 28 points (9-of-20 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, two steals, a block, and four 3-pointers in the 125-118 loss to the Rockets on Friday. 
 The Jazz have let Darryn Peterson go, and we’ve really started to see the Kansas version of Darryn Peterson come into fruition. He has started to carry more of the offense and it’s been looking good for the Jazz. They’ve been in more games, and the team really flows well. He led the team in shot attempts in this one including a big third quarter. Continue to hold and we’ll reassess his value once Lauri and JJJ get back. 
 -  Brian Taylor

 Jalen Johnson had 27 points (11-of-26 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), 11 rebounds, 10 assists and one steal against the Bulls on Friday. 
 Johnson scored 27 points, but was hardly efficient on 26 attempts from the field. He recorded a triple-double, but also had five turnovers in the overtime loss. Johnson is the Hawks’ franchise leader in triple-doubles. Atlanta has the day off Saturday before a matchup against the Bucks on Sunday.

 Ace Bailey scored 21 points (7-of-13 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, an assist, and three 3-pointers against the Rockets. 
 Bailey had some big shots in this game which helped keep the Jazz in the game. He was a +10 in a game where they lost by 7. You would want more of the peripheral stats that he’s been able to show this season, but it’s hard to complain with the production he’s given you over the course of the season.

 Alperen Şengün had a monster 43 points (17-of-24 FGs, 8-of-12 FTs), 12 rebounds, five assists, a steal, a block and a three in the 125-118 win over the Jazz on Friday.
 Şengün took advantage of the Jazz’s center situation, or lack thereof. He was a monster in this game, and the Jazz had no answers for him at all. He won’t be this good every night, but he had a great performance this season. He is shooting way over what he’s shot at any point in his career from the 3PT line, so that should come down a bit, but he’s having a career at this point and with Durant taking more of a step back, there is a lot more sustainability with what he’s doing.
 -  Brian Taylor

 Josh Giddey had 15 points (5-of-10 FGs, 2-of-5 FTs), 10 rebounds, 14 assists, three blocks and three three-pointers against the Hawks on Friday. 
 Giddey’s triple-double was his first of the season and his 21st since joining the Bulls. Only Michael Jordan (28) has more in franchise history. Giddey has made at least 44 percent of his attempts in four consecutive games after an early season shooting slump. He and the Bulls will face the Timberwolves on Saturday.

 Kevin Durant had 22 points (5-of-14 FGs, 10-of-10 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, and two 3-pointers in win over the Jazz on Friday. 
 Durant has been taking a bit of a step back this season, which is remarkable given his age that he’s still averaging 20 points per game. The shot attempts have gone down, the efficiency has gone down, the assists are down, and it’s hard to imagine that it will come back to what it was last season. It’s a good thing for Houston that they haven’t needed him to be that guy, but it looks like father time is starting to catch up with him.
 -  Brian Taylor

 Tari Eason scored 14 points (6-of-13 FGs), 11 rebounds, two assists, and two 3-pointers in win over the Jazz on Friday. 
 Eason got the minutes over Jabari Smith in this game, and he was wreaking havoc in this one. He was in the dunker spots and taking advantage of the Jazz’s lack of a high-level big man defender. It’s not a sign to add Tari Eason but more of a reassurance that he is still a good streamer if you’re looking for rebounds with the potential for a good game.
 -  Brian Taylor

 Norman Powell had 33 points (12-of-19 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal and four three-pointers in the Bulls’ 125-117 victory over the Hawks on Friday. 
 Powell led the Bulls with 33 points in the overtime victory over the Hawks Friday. The 33-year-old guard helped put the game away with an and-1 that put the Bulls up by five with less than two minutes left in overtime. It was Powell’s second game with at least 30 points this season. The Bulls will take on the Timberwolves on the second night of a back-to-back on Saturday.
